primary.title: Zn recovery from steel mill EAF dusts: A two-step biotechnological approach
primary.version: Resources, Conservation & Recycling Advances 27 (September 2025), 200278; printed available-online date 16 July 2025. Crossref version-of-record license start is 15 July 2025, not evidence of an independently revised article.
primary.inspection: All nine pages read and visually inspected as eaf-page-1.png through eaf-page-9.png, covering every Figure 1-9 and Table 1-5. Figures 1-3 provide contextual distributions, process flow and reactor layout; they are not independent performance datasets.
primary.license: CC BY-NC 4.0, printed in the PDF and confirmed by Crossref version-of-record license. PDF and renderings remain outside Git.
primary.identity: Two actual EAF dusts from an unnamed steelmaking company; country and exact mineral phases of these samples are not established. The authors’ affiliations do not supply feed location.
primary.organisms: A. thiooxidans DSM 504 produces acid upstream. Live NCBI species ID 930 and DSMZ accession checked. The downstream anode is an unresolved mixed culture from another MEC; no inferred member IDs.
primary.data_statement: Data will be made available on request. No raw per-cycle deposit/feed balance or downloadable data dictionary was acquired. No author contact was made.
primary.supplements: No supplementary appendix/link was identified in the full nine-page article or returned indexed publisher page. Direct publisher HTML returned 403; three conventional mmc1 extension probes returned 404. These are bounded failures, not proof that no supplement exists.

context_primary.title: Zinc recovery from bioleachate using a microbial electrolysis cell and comparison with selective precipitation
context_primary.inspection: Fresh full 11-page PDF acquired; relevant Methods and Analytics and calculations text read, with page 3 visually inspected for Equations 1-2. Other figures and its biological results were not comprehensively audited in this investigation.
context_primary.role: Method definition only. Equation 1 uses initial and final catholyte zinc concentration; Equation 2 is cathodic coulombic efficiency. Its distinct blast-furnace dust, graphite cathode and community are not imported as EAF observations.
context_primary.license: CC BY 4.0 printed in the primary article. Raw retained outside Git.

identifier_checks.result: Maps to Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans; confirms cited accession, not independent stock authentication.
Species Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans confirmed. No identifier applied to unresolved MEC community.

source_conflicts_and_limits.finding: Abstract Fe precipitation is 48%; Results and the plotted bar give about 42% at pH 3.8. No corrected number is invented.

source_conflicts_and_limits.locator: Tables 4-5 versus Figure 6, Dust 1 at 100 g/L and 10 minutes
source_conflicts_and_limits.finding: 9745 mg/L divided by the Table 4 dust inventory, 161000 mg/kg times 0.1 kg/L, implies about 60.5% Zn extraction. Figure 6 instead depicts about 30%. The 2-minute textual value 28.9 +/- 0.2% is not a replacement for the 10-minute datum. Other Dust 1 table/figure pairings also fail to agree; its extraction is not silently harmonized.

The purified, stated 1:1-diluted MEC feed contains 1785 mg/L Zn, whereas the best Dust 2 leachate contains 29900 mg/L. The particular preliminary batch and losses/dilution connecting them are insufficiently specified. No overall dust-to-product yield is computed.

source_conflicts_and_limits.locator: Methods 2.7 and cited Spiess 2023 Equation 1; Results 3.3
source_conflicts_and_limits.finding: 99.9 +/- 0.1% is catholyte concentration depletion over seven serial cycles, not weighed electrode yield or recovery of all dust zinc. The selected-metal ICP composition is 99.15% Zn, not a complete elemental/phase/product purity certificate.
The hydrogen peroxide wording 30 vol% does not unambiguously distinguish stock strength from amount added. No invented final peroxide concentration is assigned.

Acidity is calculated rather than titrated, reported as approximately 0.5 M with average sulfate around 50 g/L and pH 0.3. Exact per-assay acid inventories and the concentration/speciation convention are unavailable; no curator-recalibrated acidity is supplied.

Duplicate leaching assays and seven serial MEC cycles do not establish independent reactor replication. No matched reagent-acid, abiotic-anode or open-circuit comparator is reported. Broader energy and reuse comparisons are not measured advantages for this system.

correction_search: No matching correction, erratum or retraction identified in the bounded exact-DOI/title returned result sets. Crossref has no update-to and an empty relation object. These checks do not prove universal notice absence.

mechanisms: Mixed-community bioanode-associated cathodic deposition and solution depletion
curation_handoff.omitted: No inherited criticality, dust external ID, anode taxon ID, industrial deployment, overall recovery yield or exact source concentration observations. Table 4 concentrations lack an analysis date required by the native quantitative contract; qualified prose is sufficient. No schema change needed.
